 ‘Very clear’ evidence sought in VP trial
 Marc Jayson Cayabyab - The Philippine Star November 19, 2026 | 12:00am 
 Alan Peter Cayetano and Sara Duterte Ryan Baldemor / The Philippine STAR, Vice President Sara Duterte via Facebook 
 MANILA, Philippines — Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano hopes for clear evidence to help them decide whether to convict or acquit Vice President Sara Duterte, whose impeachment trial resumes today after a break due to the ASEAN Summit hosting.
 “I’m hoping the evidence will be very, very clear to acquit or very, very clear to convict,” Cayetano said in a chance interview after attending the 51st National Prayer Breakfast at Club Filipino in San Juan.
 A verdict not based on strong evidence would only “further divide the country” on such a polarizing topic, according to Cayetano, who pushed for addressing the country’s “political, spiritual and economic battle.”
 Senate impeachment court spokesman Reginald Tongol said the defense team is expected to field four witnesses today and tomorrow to testify about CALE88 Foods Corp., a banana chips manufacturer, which prosecutors alleged had received a P319-million “remittance” from Chinese companies.
 They are Rainer dela Fuente, who will testify about the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLC); Ceferino Rodolfo, Department of Trade and Industry undersecretary, who will testify on CALE88’s registration with the Board of Investments; Pilar Marilyn Pagayunan of the Food and Drug Administration, who will testify on Cale88’s FDA product registration for its sweetened banana chips, and Rowena Mendoza from the DTI Center for International Trade Expositions and Missions, or her representative, about the communications and invitations sent to CALE88 for food expositions.
 “All four are covered by requests for Subpoena Ad Testificandum and Duces Tecum to controvert allegations under Article II,” Tongol said.
 When the prosecution presented its AMLC witness, executive director Ronel Buenaventura last month, senators tackled the possibility that CALE88 may have been used for money laundering after it allegedly received funds from China.
 The Vice President’s husband Manases Carpio holds a 47.5 percent share in CALE88.
 Duterte may be convicted by the court as some senators are reportedly being “pressured,” Duterte’s spokesman Paolo Panelo claimed.
 Honest mistake? 
 The House prosecution panel did not give any weight to the claim of the Vice President that she made an “honest mistake” when she declared GenCorp. Industries as one of her business interests in her statement of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN).
 House prosecutor Manila Rep. Joel Chua and prosecution team adviser Ace Barbers pointed out that Duterte repeatedly listed the company and its predecessors in her SALN, specifically for two consecutive years. — Evelyn Macairan, Daphne Galvez
